grading_system.evidence: graduation from Danville High School is based on three benchmarks: Courses (Class of 2029 and beyond) ... Demonstrated Performance in Areas of Personal Proficiency
grading_system.min_score_to_earn_credit: 2.0 on the 4-point grade scale to earn course credit

schedule.evidence: A semester, for the purpose of documenting coursework, is defined as a single-block semester-long course. Courses that meet for 2 blocks will count as two semesters.

credit_definition.text: Requirements are counted in semesters. One semester = a single-block semester-long course; a course meeting for 2 blocks counts as two semesters. Credit is not used as the unit.
credit_definition.evidence: A semester, for the purpose of documenting coursework, is defined as a single-block semester-long course. Courses that meet for 2 blocks will count as two semesters.

course_load.evidence: Students are strongly encouraged to take courses above and beyond these minimum requirements.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Class of 2029 and beyond: 8 English + 6 Global Citizenship + 6 Math + 6 Science + 3 PE + 1 Health + 6 arts/CTE/design/engineering + 6 electives = 42 semesters. Classes of 2027-28 need 38 (2 electives). The catalog gives no conversion to standard credits (1 = full-year course), so total_in_credits is null. Also requires a yearlong Senior Capstone Project (waived for Early College students) and a MAP demonstrating the Areas of Personal Proficiency.

flexible_pathways_listed: dual-credit English and Global Citizenship courses
online courses from other providers if not offered in-house
notes: Current catalog is 2026-27. Requirements are stated in semesters, not credits, and the catalog gives no courses-per-term count, so courses_per_term is null. The regional technical center is referenced for juniors and seniors in the Woodworking/Pathways program description (p.24) but no center is named. Graduation has three benchmarks (p.4): courses, the Senior Capstone, and demonstrated performance in six Areas of Personal Proficiency (Lead, Express, Solve, Connect, Care, Achieve) via a MAP (p.4, p.6-7). The catalog states no proficiency scale. Equivalent learning opportunities (internships, work-based learning, independent study) may substitute for courses when they document proficiency (p.5).
